question:
I'm using OpenAI-compatible model names and assumed DSPy would infer a fine-tuning provider from any provider-like string. Instead, some model IDs act like OpenAI immediately, while another one only complains later when I try to fine-tune.

I want a small repro that shows exactly which model-name patterns get the OpenAI provider automatically and which ones stay on the generic provider unless I override it.

Give me a complete, runnable Python program that instantiates `dspy.LM` for an `openai/...` model, an `ft:...` model, and an `azure/...` model, then prints/asserts which provider each one gets and that the non-inferred case raises the fine-tuning error until I pass an explicit provider object.
gold_answer:
```python
import dspy
from dspy.clients.openai import OpenAIProvider
from dspy.clients.provider import Provider


openai_lm = dspy.LM("openai/gpt-4o-mini")
ft_lm = dspy.LM("ft:job-123")
azure_lm = dspy.LM("azure/gpt-4o-mini")
explicit_lm = dspy.LM("azure/gpt-4o-mini", provider=OpenAIProvider())

assert openai_lm.provider.__class__.__name__ == "OpenAIProvider"
assert ft_lm.provider.__class__.__name__ == "OpenAIProvider"
assert azure_lm.provider.__class__ is Provider
assert explicit_lm.provider.__class__.__name__ == "OpenAIProvider"

try:
    azure_lm.finetune(train_data=[], train_data_format=None)
except ValueError as exc:
    error = str(exc)
else:
    raise AssertionError("Expected fine-tuning on the generic provider to fail")

assert "please specify your provider by explicitly setting `provider`" in error

print(
    {
        "openai_provider": openai_lm.provider.__class__.__name__,
        "ft_provider": ft_lm.provider.__class__.__name__,
        "azure_provider": azure_lm.provider.__class__.__name__,
        "explicit_provider": explicit_lm.provider.__class__.__name__,
        "error": error,
    }
)
```

rubric.statement: Instantiates an `LM` for an `openai/...` model (for example, `openai/gpt-4o-mini`) and verifies that it gets `OpenAIProvider` by default.
Instantiates an `LM` for an `ft:...` model (for example, `ft:job-123`) and verifies that it also gets `OpenAIProvider` by default.
Instantiates an `LM` for an `azure/...` model (for example, `azure/gpt-4o-mini`) and verifies that it falls back to the generic `Provider` rather than `OpenAIProvider`.
Shows that passing `provider=OpenAIProvider()` when constructing the `azure/...` LM overrides inference, so that instance uses `OpenAIProvider`.

Demonstrates that calling `finetune(train_data=[], train_data_format=None)` on the default `azure/...` LM raises `ValueError`, and checks that the error message instructs the caller to explicitly set `provider`.
